mathematical_or_operational_scope: Composite-length numerical probe for a Ramanujan-sum averaged Fourier-mask matrix and its gauged block-Fourier norm. The scan covers divisors 2<=m<=sqrt(n), not every possible block shape.
positive_controls: Lines 32–34 form entries as exact Fractions; lines 65–77 compare full-matrix symmetry, trace and top eigenvalue with the block calculation on n<=100.
Lines 53–59 deduplicate equal gcd patterns and use Euler-phi weights, rather than reusing a prime-only formula.

findings.issue: The claimed bound is only screened with floating-point eigenvalues and fixed absolute/relative tolerances. There is no interval enclosure, residual-based spectral error bound, exact characteristic polynomial or certified upper-bound proof.

Formula verification is optional; the default run records formula_checks=0 and can still produce an empty counterexamples list. --max-n below 4 returns no parameter tests and worst=None without failing.
Callable routines do not enforce positive integers, m|n, m<=n, or nonempty dimensions. Main supplies the intended domain but standalone callers can silently leave the intended formula domain.

cost_and_scaling: full_exact needs O(n^2 m) summands and O(n^2) rational storage. masks allocates an m×m matrix per gcd class; each retained ell performs dense m×m Hermitian eigensolving, O(m^3), with at most n/m classes. The full max-n scan is a research experiment, not a near-linear certified transform implementation.
test_scope_and_limits: Read-only assessment of verify and main; no NumPy code executed. The finite n<=100 verification itself uses floating eigensolvers after exact entry construction. The max-n=1000 default is finite empirical evidence only.
certificate_acceptance: counterexamples=[] means no numerical violation above 1e-10 in the enumerated divisors. It does not certify the all-composite theorem, other parameter regimes, or the true norm at the tolerance boundary.
